svg.aria-label: Diagram: resource provider registration as a per-subscription, per-region state, showing which deployment paths register a provider automatically, which do not, and the two error codes that result
svg.title: Resource provider registration: a per-subscription, per-region state
svg.text: Registration is a property of your subscription, not of Azure
The service exists either way. What registration decides is whether this subscription is allowed to call it — region by region.
Registers for you
Creating a resource in the portal.
Deploying an ARM template or Bicep file — but only
for the providers actually named in that template.
Some providers are registered by default on a new
subscription, which is why the gap is invisible until
the day it is not.
You register by hand
Supporting resources a deployment creates but the
template never mentions — monitoring and security
are the usual pair.
The named example: VM auto-shutdown needs
Microsoft.DevTestLab registered, which no reading of
a VM template would ever suggest.
Registration completes region by region
The operation runs individually for every supported region. To create a resource in one region, only that region
needs to have finished. So code that waits for the state to leave Registering waits for regions it will never use —
and a provider that was registered before a new region existed needs registering again to reach it.
MissingSubscriptionRegistration
The subscription is not registered to use
namespace {resource-provider-namespace}
Says what it means: register the namespace.
NoRegisteredProviderFound
No registered resource provider found for
location {location} and API version {api-version}
Three possible causes, only one of them registration.
